== Enshrined deities ==
* It enshrines {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|it|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|ja|イシコリドメ|ru|Исикори-домэ но микото|zh|伊斯許理度賣命|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}}.
* According to the Sōma-domain historical work ''Ōsōshi'', it enshrines {{ill|Izanami|ar|إزانامي|az|İzanami|bcl|Izanami|bs|Izanami|ca|Izanami|da|Izanami|el|Ιζανάμι|eo|Izanami|es|Izanami|fa|ایزانامی|fi|Izanami|fr|Izanami|he|איזאנמי|hr|Izanami|hu|Izanami|hy|Իզանամի|id|Izanami|it|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|ka|იძანამი|ko|이자나미|mk|Изанами|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯃꯤ|pt|Izanami|rsk|Изанами|ru|Идзанами|simple|Izanami|sl|Izanami|sr|Изанами|sv|Izanami|ta|இசநமி|th|อิซานามิ|tl|Izanami|tr|Izanami|uk|Ідзанамі|zh|伊邪那美|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takakuraji|fr|Takakuraji|it|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|zh|高倉下|qid=Q11668757|lt=Kumano Takakuraji-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|it|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|kk|Такэмикадзути|ko|타케미카즈치|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|tr|Takemikazuchi|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}.
** Another theory says it enshrined Izanami-no-Mikoto, Yomotsuchi-moribito, and {{ill|Kikurihime|it|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛神|mni|ꯀꯨꯀꯨꯔꯤꯍꯤꯃꯦ|zh|菊理媛命|qid=Q11619891}}, and was called “Hakusan Sansho Gongen.”
* According to records, the sacred object is “five sun” in length.

== Origin ==
According to ''Ōsōshi'', it is said to be one of the eight shikinaisha shrines in Namekata District among the 100 shikinaisha shrines in Mutsu Province, though details of its enshrinement history are unknown. In ancient times it is said to have stood in Takakura village west of the current site (present Takakura, Haramachi Ward), with broad shrine grounds and many precinct shrines. A former site remains near Akashiba in Baba, Haramachi Ward, at the boundary of Oshikama, Baba, and Ōkido districts. The shrine grounds are thought to have become desolate from war and conflict; though rebuilt, it did not fully recover and became a small shrine.

The shrine steward at that time was young and could not respond, and the lands remained lost thereafter. Trees in the shrine area were also cut and turned into fields, and by the {{ill|Genbun|de|Genbun|fa|گنبون|fr|Ère Genbun|ja|元文|ko|겐분|ru|Гэмбун|simple|Genbun|sr|Генбун|sv|Genbun|tr|Genbun|zh|元文 (日本)|qid=Q1145754}} period those lands had become荒廃.

Before that, a man named Endō Hachirōzaemon lived in the village and set up a small shrine at the north end of the old grounds as a guardian deity. His heir and descendants are said to have lived around present Oshikama. At that time the domain gave 11 ryō 2 bu obtained by selling several hundred cedar trees from the grounds, and the shrine was restored. In {{ill|Human herpesvirus 6|ar|فيروس هربسي بشري 6|de|Humanes Herpesvirus 6|es|Human herpesvirus 6|fr|Herpèsvirus humain type 6|hi|ह्यूमेन हर्पसवाइरस ६|it|Herpesvirus umano 6|ja|ヒトヘルペスウイルス6|pt|Herpesvírus humano 6|ru|Вирусы герпеса человека 6 типа|sv|Humant herpesvirus 6|qid=Q6974}} ({{ill|Bunka|ca|Bunka|de|Bunka (Ära)|es|Bunka|fa|بونکا|fr|Ère Bunka|ia|Bunka|ja|文化 (元号)|ko|분카|ms|Zaman Bunka|ru|Бунка|simple|Bunka|sr|Бунка|sv|Bunka|tr|Bunka|zh|文化 (年號)|qid=Q1373146}} 12), by order of lord {{ill|Sōma Masutane|ja|相馬益胤|ko|소마 마스타네|qid=Q8514605}}, a survey identified this shrine as “Takakura Shrine,” one of the eight Namekata shikinaisha shrines. In that year, one koku of rice field was lent as shrine land in recognition of its history.

* The shrine buildings stand on a hill beside a river flowing through Oshikama.
